name: Process capital calls
summary: General partners of the funds the organisation has committed to send capital call notices, usually about ten business days before the money is due, by email or through their investor portals. A private markets operations analyst retrieves each notice, checks it against the commitment record and the partnership agreement, verifies the wire instructions, splits the call across the client accounts that own the interest and keys it into the private markets system. A second person checks it, the payment is approved in the custodian portal and released on the due date, and the analyst confirms and settles it. Notices come in many formats, so checking and keying are manual, and changed bank details are a known fraud risk.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about $79 billion with roughly 190 fund interests held mainly in segregated client accounts and a single global custodian.
baseline.notes: Notices handled from PDFs and portals with a private markets system and spreadsheets; no automated document extraction.

trigger: A general partner posts or emails a capital call notice for a fund in which the organisation's clients hold an interest.
end_state: The call is paid on its due date, confirmed and recorded as settled, or a duplicate is filed, or a suspected fraudulent change stops the payment.

volume.seasonality: Peaks at quarter ends, when many funds call management fees, and in December.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file. investec2022 found about 2 calls per fund per year in 2019 to 2021 in a 45-fund sample; 60 a month from about 190 interests implies nearly 4, which fits younger funds in their investment period, co-investment vehicles and calls received separately for each limited partner entity.

FTE from about 2.8 hours of analyst time per notice at 60 notices a month. Loaded cost from the organisation file, built on Job Bank Toronto wages for NOC 11101 (median $41.60 an hour, 2023-2024) deflated to 2021 with variable pay and a 1.35 loading.
Checker and payment approver. Loaded cost from the organisation file, built on Job Bank Toronto wages for NOC 10010 (median $62.37 an hour).
Foreign exchange, value-date cash check and funding shortfalls. Loaded cost from the organisation file.
Third approver for payments above the senior threshold; not in the process map roles. Loaded cost from the organisation file.

systems.name: Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Document management system and virtual data rooms
Private markets investment accounting and monitoring system (commitments, calls, distributions, valuations)
Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Electronic trading and broker platforms (equity, bond and FX multi-dealer)

steps.name: Retrieve notice from portal or mailbox
steps.description: Each morning the analyst sweeps the shared mailbox and the general partners' investor portals, each with its own login, downloads new capital call notices, saves them to the document system and checks whether the same call already arrived through another channel or replaces an earlier notice.

error.defect_description: A revised notice is treated as a new call.

evidence.note: workwise: notices are collected from portals and inboxes and duplicates matched before payment. Times and duplicate rate tier C.

steps.name: Log notice in capital activity tracker
steps.description: The analyst types the fund, limited partner entity, notice date, due date, currency and amount into the capital activity tracker so the call is visible to the team and the cash forecast.

error.defect_description: Due date or amount keyed wrongly.

evidence.note: Notices logged by fund, entity and date (workwise). Times tier C.

steps.name: Check call against commitment record
steps.description: The analyst opens the commitment record in the private markets system and checks the limited partner entity, commitment, contributions to date, unfunded balance and the share of the total call stated on the notice, and that the call does not exceed the unfunded commitment or any recallable amount.

control.basis: Private markets operations procedure: every call validated against the commitment and unfunded balance before payment

next.condition: entity, percentage or balance does not match

evidence.note: Each call compared with the commitment and prior statements (workwise); ILPA asks GPs to show each LP's percentage. Times tier C.

steps.name: Check purpose and fee calculation against partnership agreement
steps.description: The analyst checks the breakdown into investments, management fee, fund expenses and equalisation interest against the partnership agreement and side letter: recalculates the management fee for the period from the fee rate, fee base and offsets and checks that expense types are permitted. Notices in the ILPA template are quicker to check.
inputs: partnership agreement and side letter terms

error.defect_description: Fee offset or side letter fee discount missed.

evidence.note: ILPA template standardises the accounting detail of notices (ilpa_cct, 2011 version in the period); ILPA asks for fee calculation detail including offsets; ml_cc says notice detail varies by fund. Discrepancy rate tier C.

steps.name: Query general partner on discrepancy
steps.description: The analyst emails the general partner's investor relations team or fund administrator with the discrepancy (wrong entity, percentage, fee calculation or missing breakdown) and asks for an explanation or a revised notice.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for general partner reply
steps.description: The general partner or its administrator explains the figure or issues a revised notice, which the analyst then checks again from the commitment record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Compare wire instructions with verified instructions
steps.description: The analyst compares the bank, account number and beneficiary on the notice with the standing instructions verified at closing and stored for the fund. Any difference stops the payment until it is verified by phone.

control.basis: Payment fraud control: wire details on a notice must match verified standing instructions

evidence.note: Changed wire instructions are the main fraud red flag and are verified before payment. Change rate tier C.

steps.name: Verify changed bank details by call-back
steps.description: The manager calls the general partner's chief financial officer or administrator on a number already on file, never one in the notice or email, confirms the new details, obtains a signed confirmation and updates the standing instructions with a second approver. Unconfirmed changes are treated as attempted fraud.
outputs: verified new instructions or fraud report

control.basis: Call-back on a previously verified number and two-person approval of any change to standing payment instructions

next.condition: change confirmed by the general partner
change not confirmed, payment stopped and reported

evidence.note: fc_fraud: call back on a verified number and two approvers for changes to standing instructions; the organisation file's cash process also requires call-backs on new payment details. Rates tier C.

steps.name: Split call across owning accounts
steps.description: The analyst splits the limited partner's call across the client accounts or pool that own the interest, using the allocation percentages in the commitment record, resolves rounding, and notes which accounts need foreign currency.

error.defect_description: Old allocation percentages used after a client reallocation.

evidence.note: The organisation file says private interests sat in segregated client accounts, so each call is split; method tier C.

steps.name: Enter pending call in private markets system
steps.description: The analyst enters the call for each owning account in the private markets system as a pending contribution split into investment, fee and expense components, and attaches the notice.

error.defect_description: Component keyed to the wrong transaction type, misstating unfunded commitment.

evidence.note: Re-keying from PDF notices is the norm in the period per the organisation file; times tier C.

steps.name: Independent check of call record
steps.description: The manager, or a second analyst, checks the notice, the validation checklist, the split and the system entries before anything is paid, and sends errors back to the preparer.

control.basis: Maker-checker: the person who records a capital call does not approve it alone

evidence.note: No single person should initiate, approve and record a transaction (fc_fraud); a second person approves (workwise). Error rate tier C.

steps.name: Update cash forecast
steps.description: The analyst adds the payment to the cash forecast by account and value date and notifies the cash team and the total portfolio team, whose weekly liquidity forecast tracks calls against unfunded commitments.

evidence.note: ILPA asks GPs for quarterly call projections because LPs forecast calls; the organisation file links calls to liquidity forecasting. Times tier C.

steps.name: Create payment instruction at custodian
steps.description: The analyst keys a wire instruction for each paying account in the custodian portal: beneficiary from the verified instructions, amount, currency, value date and the fund's reference, and attaches the notice.

error.defect_description: Wrong value date or reference keyed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; share of foreign currency calls assumes about half of commitments are to US or European funds.

steps.name: Arrange foreign exchange for the payment
steps.description: The cash analyst books a spot foreign exchange trade for the value date with the custodian's desk or through the FX platform, sized from the call, and records it in the cash projection.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Approve payment instruction
steps.description: The manager reviews each instruction against the notice and verified instructions and releases it as second authoriser in the custodian portal under the signing authority matrix. Payments above the senior threshold need a further approver.

control.basis: Payment authorisation matrix: dual authorisation in the custodian portal, preparer cannot approve

evidence.note: Dual approval and segregation of duties (fc_fraud); the organisation file says wires above set thresholds need two approvers. Threshold share tier C.

steps.name: Senior approval of large payment
steps.description: The vice president of investment operations checks the notice and approval trail and adds the third authorisation required for large payments.

control.basis: Signing authority policy: third authoriser above the senior payment threshold

evidence.note: Threshold and approval level are assumptions.

steps.name: Hold payment until value date
steps.description: The approved wire waits in the custodian's system until its value date, which is the due date on the notice; most notices give about ten business days, so the wait depends on how fast the earlier steps ran.

evidence.note: ILPA recommends at least 10 business days to respond to a call; ml_cc says the notice period for many funds is 10 business days. The 3 to 10 day hold after approval is derived.

steps.name: Confirm cash available on value date
steps.description: In the morning cash projection the cash analyst confirms each paying account has the cash, including any FX proceeds, before the custodian's payment cut-off.

evidence.note: The organisation file's cash process says late capital call notices cause many exceptions; rate tier C.

steps.name: Arrange funding for shortfall
steps.description: The cash analyst asks the total portfolio team to raise cash, sells money market holdings or arranges a transfer between the client's accounts so the call can be paid on time.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Custodian sends the wire
steps.description: The custodian's payment system releases the wire to the general partner's bank on the value date and returns a payment reference.

evidence.note: Standard custodian payment processing.

steps.name: Confirm payment and notify general partner
steps.description: Next morning the analyst checks the debit on the custodian cash statement, records the payment reference, sends or uploads a payment confirmation where the general partner asks for one and marks the call paid in the tracker.

next.condition: general partner reports funds not received or wire returned

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Trace missing or returned payment
steps.description: The analyst asks the custodian to trace the wire, gives the general partner the payment reference, and if the wire was returned arranges a resend with fresh approvals.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Mark call settled and post
steps.description: The analyst marks the transactions settled in the private markets system, which updates contributions and the unfunded commitment and produces the accounting entries for the monthly close, and files the evidence.

evidence.note: Checked records post to the books (workwise). Times tier C.

exceptions.name: Notice discrepancy
exceptions.description: The entity, percentage, management fee or expense breakdown does not agree with the commitment record or partnership agreement; the general partner explains or reissues the notice.

exceptions.name: Changed bank details
exceptions.description: The notice shows new wire instructions; payment waits for a call-back on a known number, and about one in 25 such cases is an attempted fraud that is stopped and reported.

exceptions.name: Foreign currency call
exceptions.description: The fund calls in US dollars or euros and the cash team books FX for the value date.

exceptions.name: Funding shortfall on value date
exceptions.description: The paying account lacks cash on the due date, usually after a late or unexpected call, and the cash team raises or moves cash.

exceptions.name: Duplicate notice
exceptions.description: The same call arrives by email and portal, or a revised notice replaces an earlier one, and is filed without payment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from notice receipt to payment confirmed and settled
benchmarks.population: Capital calls on private equity, infrastructure, real estate and credit funds

evidence.note: Payment is made on the due date; 10 business days of notice (about 14 calendar days) is the ILPA recommendation and the common partnership agreement term (ml_cc). Some notices allow less time and receipt can lag issue by a day.

pain_points.description: Notices arrive through many portals and email in different layouts, so retrieving and re-keying them is manual and duplicates slip through.

evidence.note: The ILPA template exists to standardise notice content.

pain_points.description: Recalculating management fees and offsets from the partnership agreement is slow and the main source of queries.

evidence.note: ILPA asks GPs to show fee calculations including offsets.

pain_points.description: Changed wire instructions in emailed notices are a fraud vector and every change needs a call-back that can delay payment.
Calls with short or unexpected notice cause funding shortfalls and same-day scrambles in cash management.

evidence.note: The organisation file names late capital call notices as a main exception in daily cash management.

sources.title: ILPA Principles 3.0
sources.supports: Capital calls should follow the ILPA standardised format with fee and carry detail and the LP's percentage, with quarterly projections of calls; LPs should have a window of at least 10 business days to respond to capital call requests; ILPA Capital Call and Distribution Notice Template dated 2011; side letter negotiation costs can be sizeable and GPs should disclose side letters; fundraising should end within a reasonable period after initial close, for example 12 months.

sources.title: ILPA Capital Call & Distribution Template (web page)
sources.supports: Template gives visibility in a standardised format into the accounting details and transaction components of capital calls and distributions; the 2025 version replaces the 2011 template from Q1 2027, so the 2011 template applied in 2019 to 2022.

sources.title: ILPA Due Diligence Questionnaire 2.0
sources.supports: Standard LP due diligence questionnaire in 20 sections (firm, fund, succession and key persons, strategy, co-investments, GP-led secondaries, credit facilities, investment process, team, alignment, market, fund terms, governance, risk and compliance, track record, accounting and valuation, reporting, legal, data security and third parties, ESG, diversity) with a requested-documents appendix (LPA, PPM, predecessor fund reports, audited financials, examples of capital call and distribution notices); asks whether LPs get more than 10 business days' notice of capital calls and asks the GP to describe its procedures for capital movements.

sources.title: Capital Calls (Venture Capital and Private Equity Funds Deskbook series)
sources.supports: The partnership agreement sets the notice period; for many venture capital and private equity funds it is 10 business days; funds use credit facilities to bridge calls; notice content varies by fund and large institutional LPs demand more detail.

sources.title: Making the call: How often do private funds request investor capital?
sources.supports: Sample of 45 private capital funds: average capital calls per fund per year 4.6 in 2015, 2.1 in 2019, 2.3 in 2020 and 1.9 in 2021 (annualised); decline attributed to subscription credit facilities.

sources.title: 8 Ways to Strengthen Protection Against Funds Transfer Fraud
sources.publisher: First Citizens Bank fund banking insights
sources.supports: Private fund payment controls: call back on a previously verified number and never on contact details in the request; two approvers for any change to standing payment instructions; no single person initiates, approves and records a transaction; daily account monitoring.

sources.title: Capital Call, Statement and K-1 Automation for Family Offices: Where AI Helps and Where It Must Not
sources.supports: LP capital call handling: collect notices from fund portals and inboxes logged by fund, entity and date; compare each call with the commitment and prior statements; match duplicate notices (same call by portal and email, revised notices); confirm wire instructions that differ from the file by phoning a number already on file; a second person approves the payment; post checked records to the books.

sources.title: Wages: Financial Analyst near Toronto (ON), NOC 11101
sources.supports: Toronto region hourly wages low $27.97, median $41.60, high $73.57 (reference period 2023-2024).

sources.title: Wages: Finance Director near Toronto (ON), NOC 10010
sources.supports: Toronto region hourly wages low $41.21, median $62.37, high $96.15 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: One case is one notice for one fund interest; the analyst splits it across the client accounts that own the interest. If a general partner sends one notice per limited partner entity, the case count rises but time per notice falls.
About half of calls are in a foreign currency and need FX booked by the cash team; this share is an estimate.
Payment is released on the due date, so the elapsed time is set by the notice period more than by the work; the hold step absorbs whatever time is left after checks and approvals.
15% of payments exceed a senior approval threshold and need the vice president of investment operations; the threshold is not public. head_investment_operations is not in the process map roles.
Distribution notices, which some general partners net against calls, are handled in distribution-processing; netted notices are treated here as calls.
The daily cash management process also sees these wires; here the cash analyst's FX, value-date check and shortfall funding are shown as steps of the call because they are triggered by it.

Hands-on time of about 3.5 hours per notice across roles (about 2.8 for the analyst) is the author's estimate; about 1.75 FTE at 60 notices a month, within the six-person private markets operations team that also handles distributions, closings and valuations support.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file.
